# THE KEPT: WHOSE VOICES WE HAVE HEARD [color=#5E5648]Pinned. First names, or what they were called. What they said. Where you heard it. Nothing else.[/color]
### #1 first_answer (OP) // 83.04.09 So that we remember who is out there. So that when someone new comes to the clearing, we can tell them who is waiting.
[bold]Henrik.[/bold] My husband. Processor fire, last winter. Behind our hab and at the north stump. Asks for the big torch. Says my name.
### #2 reservoir_dad // 83.04.10 [bold]Pia.[/bold] Seven. The reservoir, two summers ago. At the stump, and once at our kitchen window. She laughs. The same laugh, at the same joke, a thing her uncle said at the picnic that day. She has laughed at it every night for a month. I go every night. I would go every night for the rest of my life to hear that.
### #3 c_row_widow // 83.04.12 [bold]The deep level crew.[/bold] Eleven of them, I think. Singing the tram song, the one they sang coming off shift, out of tune on the high bit like they always were. Heard from the old mine road. One voice is louder than the rest. It is my Dario. He always sang too loud.
Under the singing somebody is humming. Not the tram song. A nervous little tune from the festival, the same few bars over and over. I do not know whose boy that is. If you lost someone off the deep level second shift, the families keep a thread at [netlink="lastseen.deep" link="lastseen.deep/shifts"]. Somebody there might know the tune.
### #4 two_lamps // 83.05.14 Two young voices at the north treeline. One trying to build a fire and asking for the lighter. One saying [italic]is it on, hello, hello[/italic]. We think they are the two campers from the recorder on the other board. Read it at [netlink="dontanswer.deep" link="dontanswer.deep/recording"] if you can stand to.
They sound happy. They are together. That has to count for something.
### #5 sap_and_saw // 83.05.14 Another one for your list. A man coughing, from the ridge above the valley. [italic]Over here, old son, give me a hand with this.[/italic] It is on the other board too, at [netlink="dontanswer.deep" link="dontanswer.deep/hunter"].
That man is not dead. He moved into town with his partner. He is alive and well and he has not set foot near the trees since.
It does not only keep the dead. It keeps whatever it hears. Put that at the top of your list.
### #6 ember_keeper // 83.05.15 I keep the other fire. You know who I am. I am not going to tell you to stop. You have heard that from me already, and from better people than me. I came to ask you one honest question, and I would like one honest answer.
When it speaks to you in the voice of someone you lost, does it ever say anything they did not say near these trees?
Because if it does not, it is not keeping your dead. It is keeping the last thing they said where it could hear them. And the only reason anybody ever stands where it can hear them is because it wants them to.
### #7 first_answer (OP) // 83.05.15 Thank you for asking honestly. Henrik says my name. He never said my name near the trees. He said it to me in our bed.
Make of that what you like.
### #8 c_row_widow // 83.05.16 The deep level song has a new voice in it. It is a woman. She sings on the high bit perfectly, every time, like nobody I ever knew. I have been trying for a month to work out who she is. Tonight I finally recognised it.
It is me. I sing along, at the stump. I did not know I was so good.
### #9 reservoir_dad // 83.05.17 Pia asked me something tonight. Not the laugh. A question. She said, [italic]Daddy, why were you not there.[/italic]
I never said that out loud near the trees. I never said it out loud anywhere. I have only ever said it inside my own head, every night, for two years.
I told her I was there now. I am not going home tonight. I am going to sit at the stump until she asks me again.
[color=#5E5648][italic]If your person is on [netlink="lastseen.deep" link="lastseen.deep"], someone at the stump may have heard them. Post their name below. Somebody will listen for it.[/italic][/color]
